summary: Hiroko Matsuoka works in Indology and philosophy. She was a doctoral student at Hiroshima University (attested 2006) and held a post at Leipzig University (attested 2016).

Hiromasa Tosaki was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Harvard under Daniel H. H. Ingalls, and earned his PhD at Kyushu University, studying under Satkari Mookerjee, Shoren Ihara, Ryusho Hikata, and Seiren Matsunami. He was a professor at Kyushu University (~1979–1994).
Hiromi Habata specializes in Buddhist studies and Indology. She received a PhD from the University of Freiburg and held a researcher post at the University of Munich (attested 2014).
Hiromi Yoshimura is a scholar in Buddhist studies. He taught Nobumichi Kusumoto and held posts at Ryukoku University, including lecturer (attested 1987) and an affiliation attested in 2006.
Hiromu Kitanishi was a scholar of Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology. He studied at Otani University and later served as a professor there (~1968–1991).
Hironori Tanaka specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a PhD student at Bukkyo University (attested 2015–2020) and also held a post there.

Hiroo Kashiwagi is a Buddhist studies scholar who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1958–1963). He served as a professor at Matsusaka University (~1982–1998) and president of Matsusaka Women's Junior College.

Hiroo Sato specializes in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Tohoku University (~1973–1977), held a post at Morioka College (~1984–1987), and served as a professor at Tohoku University (~1997–2019).

Hiroshi Aoyagi is a linguist who studied at International Christian University and earned a PhD from the University of Southern California (~1993–1998). He served as a professor at Nanzan University (~2007).

Hiroshi Araki specializes in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He earned his degrees, including a PhD, at Kyoto University. His career includes posts at Osaka University and as a professor at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2010–2025).
Hiroshi Deguchi studied at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1953) and later held a post at Hokkaido University (~1957–1963).

Hiroshi Kanno specializes in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo and served as director of the International Research Institute for Advanced Buddhology (~2001–2009) and vice director at The Institute of Oriental Philosophy (~2011).

Hiroshi Kuroda specializes in Indology and philosophy. He completed doctoral coursework at Kyoto University in 1976 and served as an associate professor at Osaka Gakuin University (~1983) and Osaka Gakuin Junior College (attested 1988).

Hiroshi Marui is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He studied at the University of Tokyo, Pune University, and under Albrecht Wezler. His posts include lecturer at Musashino Women's Junior College and associate professor at the University of Tokyo (1992, 1995, 1999–2018).
Hiroshi Maruyama was a scholar of Indology who served as a professor at Osaka University (attested 1987) and led the Ayurveda Research Society (attested 1987).
Hiroshi Nemoto specializes in Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He earned an MA at Hiroshima University and later served as a professor there (attested 2015).
Hiroshi Yamashita is an Indology and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Madras. He served as an associate professor at Tohoku University (attested 1996–1999).
Hisanosuke Izui was a linguist who studied at Kyoto University (~1927–1930). He held a post at Kyoto Sangyo University (~1969–1983).

Hisao Inagaki was a Buddhist studies scholar who completed a PhD at the University of London. He taught Japanese Buddhism at SOAS (1969–1981) and served as a professor at Ryukoku University (1981–1998).

Hisao Kanaseki studied at Doshisha University (~1937–1941). He was a professor at Kobe University (~1961–1967), professor emeritus at Tokyo Metropolitan University (~1967–1982), and professor at Komazawa University (~1982–1993).
